guide.title: Lyndon Outing Club, Vermont: Shonya Hill's T-bar, rebuilt after lightning
guide.intro: Lyndon Outing Club dates to at least 1926, when the first Winter Carnival was held in Lyndonville, per New England Ski History's Lyndon Outing Club page. The club was formally organized in late 1936 or early 1937, with Milton Kerr as president, and grew to 106 members by the winter of 1936-37. The ski area sits on Shonya Hill, east of Lyndonville village, and is run strictly by volunteers, who handle lift operation, concessions, and grooming, according to the New England Lost Ski Areas Project's Lyndon Outing Club page.

sections.heading: From a lighted slope to Shonya Hill
sections.body: On January 2, 1938 the club debuted a lighted ski slope on Oscar Baril's farm near Fletcher School, headlined by national ski jumping champion Clarence Olesen, per New England Ski History's Lyndon Outing Club page. The club installed a 10-horsepower, 375-foot electric rope tow on December 23, 1939. In 1947 the club relocated to Shonya Hill on land provided by the Shonyo family; a new 800-foot rope tow debuted there in mid-December 1947, with Fred Hansen, later the designer of Mount Sunapee, assisting in selecting the site.

sections.heading: The T-bar, twice rebuilt
sections.body: During the 1961-62 season, club members built a 1,600-foot T-bar lift to mark the club's 25th anniversary, dedicated with a week-long carnival of races, a ball, a torchlight parade, and fireworks in February 1962, per New England Ski History's Lyndon Outing Club page. After the club's T-bar was struck by lightning around 1982, the club secured an $18,000 town loan to purchase a replacement T-bar from Stowe. A T-bar malfunction forced a mid-winter shutdown in 2011; volunteers restored the lift in time for the 2011-12 season. In 2021 the club received a $26,000 grant from the Northern Forest Center to support mountain bike trail development.

sections.heading: Nearby covered bridges
sections.body: Built in 1871, the Old Schoolhouse Bridge is believed to be the only surviving 19th-century covered bridge with covered walkways on both sides, per Wikipedia's Old Schoolhouse Bridge article. It was listed on the National Register of Historic Places on March 31, 1971 (NRHP reference No. 71000055) and carried vehicle traffic until 1973. Chamberlin Mill Covered Bridge carries Chamberlin Bridge Road across the South Wheelock Branch of the Passumpsic River in a rural-residential area of south-central Lyndon, and was listed on the National Register of Historic Places on July 30, 1974 (NRHP reference No. 74000205), per Wikipedia's Chamberlin Mill Covered Bridge article.

faq.question: Who runs Lyndon Outing Club?
faq.answer: The club is run strictly by volunteers, who handle lift operation, concessions, and grooming, per the New England Lost Ski Areas Project's Lyndon Outing Club page. It dates to at least 1926 and was formally organized in late 1936 or early 1937.

faq.question: What happened to the T-bar after it was struck by lightning?
faq.answer: After the club's T-bar was struck by lightning around 1982, the club secured an $18,000 town loan to purchase a replacement T-bar from Stowe, per New England Ski History's Lyndon Outing Club page. A later T-bar malfunction forced a mid-winter shutdown in 2011, and volunteers restored the lift in time for the 2011-12 season.
